lesson.subtitle: Lesson 10 -- The China Delegation
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Luciana Galleote Cartocci | Lesson 10 -- The China Delegation
lesson.grammar_point: be going to vs present continuous for future plans and fixed arrangements (the plan of a business trip)

listenings.text: Hello everyone, I am Anjali, and I organize business trips to China for hospital groups. Let me explain how our trips work. The flights, the hotels and the main visits are always booked before you leave. So, if your itinerary says that you are visiting a factory on Tuesday at nine, that is fixed, and the host is waiting for you. But every delegation also has some free time, and my advice is to decide early what you are going to do with it. Some people are going to rest, and that is fine, because jet lag is hard in the first two days. Others are going to visit a showroom or meet a partner. Just tell me a week before, and I will try to organize it.

Hello Luciana, this is Wei Zhang from the international sales team in Shenzhen. I am calling about your visit next month. Everything is ready on our side. My colleague is picking up your group at the hotel at eight thirty on Tuesday, and we are starting the factory tour at nine. After lunch, we are showing you our new cameras in the showroom. In the evening, our director is having dinner with the delegation. We are also bringing an interpreter, so the doctors in your group can ask questions in Portuguese. I have one question for you: are you going to bring your engineers? If yes, please send me their names before Friday. Thank you, and see you soon.

I went to China with a hospital delegation last year, and next spring I am going to do it again. This time, I am going to do three things differently. First, I am going to study the list of companies before the trade show. There are too many booths, and last year I walked for two days without a plan. Second, I am going to bring more business cards. I gave away two hundred in three days! And third, I am going to arrive one day early. My flight is already booked: I am leaving Paris on a Friday, and our first meeting is on Monday. That gives me time to recover from the jet lag.

vocab.title: Match each word to its meaning
defs: a small area at a trade show where a company shows its products
a person who translates what people say while they are talking
a short stop at an airport between two flights
a person or company that receives visitors and takes care of them
a detailed plan of a trip, with dates, places and times
the tired feeling after a long flight to a different time zone
a visit to see how a company makes its products
a big event where companies show their new products to buyers

paras: Next October, a delegation of twelve people from our hospital group is traveling to China. We are flying from São Paulo on the night of October 9, with a layover in Dubai, and we are landing in Shenzhen on October 11. The trip is ten days long, and the itinerary is almost ready: our hosts in China are organizing the visits, the hotels and the interpreters.

In Shenzhen, we are visiting a big medical technology trade show on October 12 and 13. More than a thousand companies are going to have a booth there, so each person in the delegation is going to focus on one area: imaging, robots, or security and video. On October 14, a camera manufacturer is taking us on a factory tour, and in the afternoon we are seeing its new showroom.

On October 15, the group is taking the train to Shanghai. The plan there is more open. Some of us are going to visit two hospitals that use artificial intelligence, and others are going to meet possible partners. Our advice to everyone: bring a lot of business cards, sleep on the plane, and do not plan important meetings on the first day. China is eleven hours ahead of São Paulo, and jet lag is real.
